research_question: Do statistically extreme completed one-minute XAUUSD returns, detected causally with the Lee-Mykland local bipower-variation jump test, exhibit enough immediate post-jump reversal to survive frozen P75 execution over 30 seconds?
source_basis: Lee & Mykland (2008) nonparametric jump test: return divided by prior local bipower variation, with Gumbel maximum-statistic rejection rule.
Lee-Mykland recommended local-volatility window for 1-minute sampling: K=603.
FX jump literature reports post-jump reversal/liquidity-provider response, motivating a single fade profile.
Gold high-frequency literature documents rare, extreme intraday jump events and uses 1/3/5/10-minute jump detection robustness.

frozen_signal.local_variance: mean of |r_j|*|r_{j-1}| over prior K-2 products, excluding current return
frozen_signal.entry: first executable P75 tick at/after completed M1 bar right edge

failure_rule: If the single preregistered M1 99% jump-fade profile fails supply/day or direct-net gate, retire LMJF rather than rescue it on Stage-A.
advance_rule: If it passes the preregistered gates, freeze unchanged for independent later-January validation.
